tasks.spec:
You are a code worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit, push or touch .git. Do NOT run a formatter on YAML or markdown (run `uv run ruff format` on Python files you change; if uv is unavailable use the repo .venv python with PYTHONPATH=.). You own only: tests/test_narration_corpus.py (new), tests/fixtures/narration_corpus_verdicts.json (new), scripts/regenerate_narration_corpus_verdicts.py (new), scripts/extract_narration_corpus.py (new), docs/testing-runbook.md (edit one existing entry only, see below). tests/fixtures/narration_corpus.json already exists: DO NOT edit it. Edit nothing else. You change no engine code and add no story nouns anywhere in code.

Goal: a permanent hermetic regression test that catches any change which makes the narration safety scan reject ordinary narration that real players already saw accepted. Background: three times a change to aliases, entities or leak terms newly rejected ordinary narration in other scenes and was found only by hand. tests/fixtures/narration_corpus.json holds 479 unique narrations (fields id, scene, input, text) that the hosted game accepted in blind-player runs, across scenes 1A to 3C of the story in data/stories/continuity-initiative. 'text' is the narration the player saw (narrator prose plus any appended authored delivery text).

Design (follow it):
1. The state builder. For each corpus entry build a RuntimeState for its scene exactly like tests/test_narration_safety.py test_ordinary_scene_wording_is_not_a_leak does (RuntimeState.bootstrap(PACKAGE), current_scene_id, phase from the scene metadata, state._assert_scene_entry_fact(scene)). Then make it a realistic late-scene state so earned vocabulary is not falsely rejected: for every knowledge item whose available_in_scenes contains ONLY scenes that come BEFORE the entry's scene (use the scene order in PACKAGE.scenes), assert its `establishes` operations into state.facts (apply the 'assert' ops; look at how KnowledgeProjector._committed_for in storygame/runtime/knowledge.py decides an item is committed and match it; also assert any scene-entry facts of the earlier scenes with state._assert_scene_entry_fact). Do not make any item of the entry's own scene earned. Reuse one builder function for every entry; build the package once at module level.
2. The verdict. For each entry run the same validation the engine runs on a proposal containing one narration segment with the entry's text: either RuntimeEngine(state, provider).turn(entry['input']) with a stub provider returning that single segment and selected_knowledge_ids [] (copy test_ordinary_scene_wording_is_not_a_leak), or call the narration validator directly if that is faster and equivalent. Verdict is 'ok' or the ProposalValidationError code (for example narration_known_term_leak). Wrap each entry so one error type cannot stop the others.
3. Golden snapshot. tests/fixtures/narration_corpus_verdicts.json maps entry id to verdict, generated by scripts/regenerate_narration_corpus_verdicts.py (`uv run python scripts/regenerate_narration_corpus_verdicts.py` rewrites the file from the current code; it prints how many entries are ok and how many are rejected, by code). Generate it from the CURRENT code and commit-ready. Entries that are rejected in the golden are false alarms of the offline state (the live game accepted them): keep them in the snapshot; they are not failures.
4. The test, tests/test_narration_corpus.py: (a) the fixture and the snapshot have identical id sets (stale snapshot fails with a message telling the developer to run the regenerate script); (b) no entry whose golden verdict is 'ok' now gets any rejection (list every offender with scene, id, code and the first 80 characters of its text; the message must say that an intentional new guard requires regenerating the snapshot in the same change and reviewing the diff); (c) a sanity test that at least 90 percent of entries are 'ok' in the golden (if your builder gives less, improve the builder before relaxing this; report the achieved rate in notes.md). Entries rejected in the golden that become 'ok' do not fail; print nothing for them.
5. scripts/extract_narration_corpus.py: usage `uv run python scripts/extract_narration_corpus.py RUN_DIR [RUN_DIR ...]` reads e2e-blind-player-r*.json files (skip names containing 'prompts') in each dir, collects turns that have scene_id, input, text and rejected false, dedupes by (scene, text), merges into tests/fixtures/narration_corpus.json (keep existing entries, add new ones, id = first 12 hex of sha1(scene + newline + text), sorted by scene then text, same JSON indent as the existing file), and prints how many were added. Run it once against nothing to check it imports; do not change the fixture.
6. docs/testing-runbook.md: find the existing entry about the narration safety scan or the narrator leak checks (search 'narration_safety' or 'leak'); edit that entry in place with at most three short lines saying the corpus test exists, how to regenerate the snapshot, and how to add runs with the extract script. Do not add dates, counts or results. If no such entry exists, add one short entry under the nearest heading about hermetic tests.

Speed: the whole test file must run in under 20 seconds on this machine (measure with `time`). If it is slower, validate directly instead of through the engine, or cache work per scene.

Run: `TMPDIR=/tmp uv run python scripts/regenerate_narration_corpus_verdicts.py` then `TMPDIR=/tmp uv run pytest -q tests/test_narration_corpus.py tests/test_narration_safety.py` (if uv is unavailable use the repo .venv python with PYTHONPATH=.). Write ./notes.md with: the achieved ok rate, entries rejected in the golden by code and scene (first ten), the runtime, and any design choice you changed and why.
